newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu and opposition leader in war of words.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu and opposition leader in war of words.

text.p: Benjamin Netanyahu struck back on Thursday at his main opposition rival, Labour party leader Ehud Barak, for saying that the prime minister's dead brother -- a national hero in Israel -- would be ashamed of him today.
"I heard a small slander from a little man," a visibly angry Netanyahu said in a speech to activists in his Likud party.
A war of words with Barak, a former army chief who was also Netanyahu's commanding officer in a crack commando unit, erupted during a no-confidence debate in parliament on Tuesday.

Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi said in the Knesset that Barak had "fled" the scene of a 1992 army training accident, leaving soldiers wounded in the field. Barak, who was chief of staff at the time, has denied the allegation.

Hanegbi's comments drew criticism from opposition and government legislators. Netanyahu distanced himself only slightly from his minister's remarks, saying he would have phrased them "a little differently".
An angry Barak retaliated on Wednesday.
"I knew another Netanyahu...Yoni Netanyahu. I am telling you Bibi, he would be ashamed of you today. I am also ashamed, along with the entire public," Barak said in a television interview.
Yonatan (Yoni) Netanyahu was the only Israeli commando killed in the 1976 rescue of Israeli passengers held hostage in Entebbe, Uganda by the Palestinian and German hijackers of an Air France plane.
Accusing Barak of going beyond the boundaries of political argument, Netanyahu said: "It is not something a decent man would have done."
Barak gave no immediate response to Netanyahu's remarks. But a Labour party spokesman said it was time for the prime minister to stop slandering Barak and "start doing his job".
